proof_summary: Lucas congruences pair the terms in the two base-[1mp[0m blocks to show both sequences vanish modulo \(p\) at every index \(p+r\) with \(0\le r<p\), making the Hankel matrices anti-triangular; meanwhile \(\binom{p-1}{k}\equiv(-1)^k\) gives anti-diagonal values \(1\) and \((-1)^{(p-1)/2}\), respectively (in the latter case all but the middle term vanish through a central-binomial divisibility argument). The determinant is therefore the product of the constant anti-diagonal and the reversal sign \((-1)^{p(p-1)/2}\), yielding the two claimed residues after sign cancellation.
